questions.stem: In this task, you are to write an essay on the necessity of developing social skills for college students. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
In today's interconnected campus life, the necessity of developing social skills for college students can hardly be overstated. Far from being an optional extra, the ability to communicate and cooperate is indispensable to a student's growth.

To begin with, strong social skills lie at the heart of academic success. Much college learning happens through group projects, seminars and lab work, where students who express ideas clearly and listen to others achieve far more than those who work in isolation. Moreover, these skills pave the way for future careers. Employers today value teamwork and communication as highly as professional knowledge, and graduates who can network and collaborate stand out in interviews. Equally important, good social skills help students build friendships, ease loneliness and adapt to campus life smoothly.

Therefore, developing social skills is by no means a trivial matter but a genuine necessity for every college student. Universities and students alike should treat it as seriously as academic study, so that young people can thrive both on campus and beyond.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 本场次听力只有一份音频，本套听力与同场第一套同卷；原文、题目与答案取自该套真题。考场多套卷的选项顺序可能不同，这里沿用第一套的顺序。在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: Operations at one of Australia's largest gold mines had to be temporarily suspended on Friday after a partial wall collapse at one of the mine's dams.
transcript.zh: 周五,澳大利亚最大的金矿之一因其中一座尾矿坝发生部分坝体垮塌而不得不暂时停止运营。

transcript.text: The wall collapse at the Cadia mine came just a few days after two earthquakes hit the area.
transcript.zh: Cadia矿区的坝体垮塌发生在该地区遭受两次地震袭击后仅数天。

transcript.text: The damage to the dam wall was noticed in the late afternoon on Friday when workers found a section of the northern dam wall had collapsed into the southern dam.
transcript.zh: 周五傍晚,工作人员发现北坝的一段坝体已坍塌至南坝中,从而注意到坝体受损。

transcript.text: The dams contain waste products of mining and can contain materials which are harmful to the environment and human health.
transcript.zh: 这些尾矿坝容纳采矿废弃物,可能含有对环境和人类健康有害的物质。

transcript.text: The dams are generally constructed using earth-fill and are gradually raised over time.
transcript.zh: 这些尾矿坝通常采用土石填筑建造,并随时间逐步加高。

transcript.text: The company was unable to confirm whether the recent earthquakes had contributed to the dam's wall collapse, but said it was conducting a thorough investigation.
transcript.zh: 该公司无法确认近期地震是否导致了坝体垮塌,但表示正在进行彻底调查。

transcript.text: A company spokesperson said the operations at the site had been halted while the investigation is ongoing and that the break had posed no safety threat to workers.
transcript.zh: 公司发言人表示,在调查期间该矿区的运营已被暂停,且此次坝体坍塌未对工作人员构成安全威胁。

questions.stem: What happened at one of Australia's largest gold mines?

options.text: Part of its dam wall collapsed.
It released a lot of harmful gases.
It was destroyed by an earthquake.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Operations at one of Australia's largest gold mines had to be temporarily suspended on Friday after a partial wall collapse at one of the mine's dams.信号：新闻导语首句锁定核心事件 。Operations at one of Australia's largest gold mines had to be temporarily suspended on Friday …

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音第 4 段 materials which are harmful to the environment and human health 出现了 harmful 这个词，但说的是「坝里盛着的矿渣可能对环境与人体有害」，并非「这次事件释放了有害气体」。选项 B 把 harmful 这个原词盗过来，再加上原文从未提及的 gases，制造了「听到 harmful 就选」的诱惑。 借用原文：The wall collapse at the Cadia mine came just a few days after two earthquakes hit the area.
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音第 2 段 The wall collapse at the Cadia mine came just a few days after two earthquakes hit the area. 只说「坝塌发生在两次地震几天之后」，并未说「金矿被地震毁了」；第 6 段更明说 The company was unable to confirm whether the recent earthquakes had contributed to the dam's wall collapse——连地震是否与坝塌有关都未确认。选项 C 把 earthquakes 这个原词盗过来，硬生生升级成「被地震毁」，是典型的过度推断。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：录音从头到尾只讲「坝体局部坍塌、暂停作业、调查中」，第 7 段反而明说 the break had posed no safety threat to workers——发言人特意说事故对工人没有安全威胁。选项 D 描述的「矿工被困井下」完全是矿难常见画面，凭考生的「常识联想」来骗人，原文无任何依据。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a partial wall collapse at one of the mine's dams ↔ Part of its dam wall collapsed. 名词化 ↔ 主谓化）

questions.evidenceText: Operations at one of Australia's largest gold mines had to be temporarily suspended on Friday after a partial wall collapse at one of the mine's dams.

questions.stem: What did the spokesperson say about the incident?

options.text: It posed a safety threat to the miners.
It caused damage too heavy to assess.
It brought the mine's operations to a halt.
It was followed by two more earthquakes.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P7）：A company spokesperson said the operations at the site had been halted while the investigation is ongoing and that the break had posed no safety threat to workers.信号：spokesperson said 引述信号词 。第 7 段开头 A company spokesperson said 是最强的引述信号，直接告诉考生「下面这句就是发言人的原话」。句中包含两个并列宾语从句（halt…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：录音第 7 段明确说 the break had posed no safety threat to workers——发言人特意强调「没有」构成安全威胁。选项 A 把 posed、safety threat 这几个高辨识度原词原样照搬，唯独把 no 去掉，含义彻底反转。这是听力里最经典的「否定词陷阱」。 借用原文：said it was conducting a thorough investigation
optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：录音第 6 段说 said it was conducting a thorough investigation——公司正在做全面调查；选项 B 却把「在调查」升级成「损失大到无法评估」 It caused damage too heavy to assess.，凭空加上了 too heavy to assess 这一程度判断，原文无任何依据。 借用原文：The wall collapse at the Cadia mine came just a few days after two earthquakes hit the area.
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音第 2 段说 The wall collapse at the Cadia mine came just a few days after two earthquakes hit the area.——坝塌发生在两次地震「之后」（事件 ← 两次地震在前）；选项 D It was followed by two more earthquakes. 却说「这次事件之后又有两次地震」，时序刚好相反，更多了 more 这个原文没有的词。选项 D 把 two earthquakes 这个原词盗过来，把时序对调。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the operations at the site had been halted ↔ It brought the mine's operations to a halt. 被动 ↔ 主动 + 动词名词化）

transcript.text: Two boys and four girls were born on Monday to the surprise of a young couple and doctors who had expected five babies.
transcript.zh: 周一,一对年轻夫妇和原本预期会有五个婴儿的医生们惊讶地迎来了两个男孩和四个女孩的诞生。

transcript.text: This was the first record of six babies being born at the same time in that region. The doctors prepared from early in the morning to help deliver five tiny citizens. They were in the operating room with five teams of doctors, one for each baby.
transcript.zh: 这是该地区首次有六个婴儿同时出生的记录。医生们从清晨就开始准备协助接生五个小公民。他们在手术室里准备了五组医生团队,每个婴儿配备一组。

transcript.text: The first five babies were delivered successfully, and all baby beds were occupied. And then all of a sudden, it turned out there was another waiting to come out.
transcript.zh: 前五个婴儿成功分娩,所有婴儿床都被占用了。然后突然之间,发现还有另一个婴儿等待出生。

transcript.text: The doctor said the babies were in healthy condition, but could not go home immediately. They needed to stay in the hospital for two to three months for medical supervision.
transcript.zh: 医生表示婴儿们健康状况良好,但不能立即回家。他们需要在医院接受两到三个月的医学监护。

transcript.text: The mother who is in stable condition could return home a day later if all physical tests came back normal. The babies' mother commented that they had already prepared room for five babies at home, so they will have to rearrange things for their happy surprise. The new parents have yet to name the sixth baby but are considering either Lily or Rose.
transcript.zh: 状况稳定的母亲如果所有体检结果正常,一天后就可以回家。婴儿的母亲表示他们已经在家里为五个婴儿准备了房间,所以他们必须为这个惊喜重新安排。这对新父母尚未给第六个婴儿取名,但正在考虑Lily或Rose。

questions.stem: What did the hospital do for the delivery of the babies?

options.text: It prepared beds for all the six new citizens.
It assigned a team of doctors for each expected baby.
It made ample preparations for various possibilities.
It brought in the most advanced instruments.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The doctors prepared from early in the morning to help deliver five tiny citizens. They were in the operating room with five teams of doctors, one for each baby.信号：动词 prepared 直接对接题干 do 。题干问 do，录音里出现 The doctors prepared from early in the morning——同一语义场的动词 prepared 就是答案信号…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：It prepared beds for all the six new citizens. 把"六个新公民都准备了床"安在医院头上，但录音 all baby beds were occupied. And then all of a sudden, it turned out there was another waiting to come out 说前五张床被占满后突然来了第六个，恰恰证明医院只准备了五张床，第六个是意外。选项里的 six 是听到的原词，却用在错误事实上。 借用原文：all of a sudden, it turned out there was another waiting to come out
optionAnalysis.C: It made ample preparations for various possibilities. 听起来像"做了充分应对各种可能性的准备"，但录音里没有任何"应对多种可能性"的话——医院其实只按五个宝宝准备，第六个是意外，恰恰说明它并未为"各种可能"做准备。这是用空泛大词诱选的典型。
optionAnalysis.D: It brought in the most advanced instruments. 说医院引进了最先进的仪器，可录音通篇都没提到任何 instrument 或 advanced 之类的词，纯属无中生有。最高级 the most 一旦录音里没有等值表述就不能选。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（five teams of doctors, one for each baby ↔ a team of doctors for each expected baby one for each baby ↔ a team for each baby）

questions.evidenceText: The doctors prepared from early in the morning to help deliver five tiny citizens. They were in the operating room with five teams of doctors, one for each baby.

questions.stem: What did the doctor say about the newborns?

options.text: They had to undergo 2-3 physical checkups.
They were all of normal size except the sixth.
They could go home together with their mother a day later.
They needed to stay in the hospital for a couple of months.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：The doctor said the babies were in healthy condition, but could not go home immediately. They needed to stay in the hospital for two to three months for medical supervision.信号：the doctor said 直接领出答案句 。录音里出现的 The doctor said 完美对应题干中的 the doctor say，紧接着的 but 转折引出真正落点：could not go home …

optionAnalysis.A: 偷换概念：They had to undergo 2-3 physical checkups. 把录音里听到的 two to three 借走，却安在 physical checkups（体检次数）上——可录音里 two to three 修饰的是 months（月数）。这是把同一数字偷换修饰对象的典型原词陷阱。 借用原文：The mother who is in stable condition could return home a day later
optionAnalysis.B: They were all of normal size except the sixth. 说"除第六个外都是正常大小"，但录音里医生只说 the babies were in healthy condition（健康），并未提任何"大小是否正常"，更没说第六个例外。这是"加细节诱选"。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：They could go home together with their mother a day later. 把"一天后回家"安在宝宝身上，但录音 The mother who is in stable condition could return home a day later 明确指出 a day later 是妈妈的安排；而宝宝那边是 could not go home immediately。选项盗用了 a day later 这个原词，把妈妈的待遇张冠到宝宝头上。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（needed to stay in the hospital for two to three months ↔ They needed to stay in the hospital for a couple of months. two to three months ↔ a couple of months）

questions.evidenceText: The doctor said the babies were in healthy condition, but could not go home immediately. They needed to stay in the hospital for two to three months for medical supervision.

transcript.text: A Spanish island called Palmador has been bought by a family from Europe for 18 million euros. The island is often described as heaven on earth by holidaymakers.
transcript.zh: 一座名为Palmador的西班牙岛屿已被一个欧洲家族以1800万欧元购得。这座岛屿常被度假者形容为人间天堂。

transcript.text: For decades tourists have been flocking to Palmador, which is located off the southeast coast of Spain. They come to enjoy its unspoiled beaches and crystal clear waters. Its natural beauty is protected as it lies inside a natural park.
transcript.zh: 数十年来，游客纷纷涌向位于西班牙东南海岸外的Palmador岛。他们来此享受未受破坏的海滩和清澈见底的海水。由于该岛位于自然公园内,其自然美景受到保护。

transcript.text: Although Palmador is one of the most famous private islands in the world, its seafront is public land and is a favorite destination for famous people. When the island was put up for sale, it was offered to the local government but proved too expensive for the local authorities. It is unclear whether the new owners have the power to ban tourists from the island. But with their newfound luxury comes the responsibility for its protection and maintenance. The island is less than two miles long and half a mile wide. It is said to have a remarkable location that few other private islands of this size can match, according to estate agents. Palmador is the perfect place to retreat to, somewhere to get away from the city noise and relax in beautiful surroundings with zero stress.
transcript.zh: 尽管Palmador是世界上最著名的私人岛屿之一,但其海滨属于公共土地,是名人最喜爱的目的地。当该岛挂牌出售时,曾提供给当地政府,但对当地政府来说价格过于昂贵。目前尚不清楚新业主是否有权禁止游客登岛。但随着新获得的奢华享受,他们也肩负着保护和维护该岛的责任。该岛长度不到两英里,宽度半英里。据房地产经纪人称,该岛拥有卓越的地理位置,少有其他同等规模的私人岛屿能与之媲美。Palmador是完美的隐居之地,可以远离城市喧嚣,在美丽的环境中放松身心,毫无压力。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about the Spanish island Palmador?

options.text: It is owned by the local government.
It has been turned into a public park.
It has been bought by an American.
It is a perfect tourist destination.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A Spanish island called Palmador has been bought by a family from Europe for 18 million euros. The island is often described as heaven on earth by holidaymakers.信号：新闻导语+总括赞美句 。答案信号有两层：一是开头第一句作为新闻导语，交代核心事实「a family from Europe（欧洲家庭）买下了岛」；二是紧接的总括赞美 often described as heaven…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项说岛 owned by the local government，但原文 has been bought by a family from Europe 与第三段 it was offered to the local government but proved too expensive for the local authorities 明确说「曾打算卖给地方政府，但地方政府嫌太贵买不起」——所以买家是欧洲家庭，不是政府，A 反了。 借用原文：its natural beauty is protected as it lies inside a natural park
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：原文只说「它位于一个 natural park 里面」（its natural beauty is protected as it lies inside a natural park），是说岛位于自然公园之内、受保护；并没有说岛本身「被变成了公共公园」。选项 turned into a public park 偷换了「位于公园内」和「自身变成公园」。 借用原文：has been bought by a family from Europe
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：原文 has been bought by a family from Europe 明确说买家来自欧洲（Europe），选项 bought by an American 把国籍换成了美国人——动作（bought）原音照搬，国籍偷换，是典型的「原词陷阱+张冠李戴」组合。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（often described as heaven on earth by holidaymakers ↔ a perfect tourist destination 总括赞美·同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: A Spanish island called Palmador has been bought by a family from Europe for 18 million euros. The island is often described as heaven on earth by holidaymakers.

questions.stem: What do holidaymakers come to Palmador to enjoy?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：For decades tourists have been flocking to Palmador, which is located off the southeast coast of Spain. They come to enjoy its unspoiled beaches and crystal clear waters.信号：原音 come to enjoy 直接点题 。答案信号是原音里 They come to enjoy its unspoiled beaches and crystal clear waters 出现的 come t…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：全文未出现任何与 seafood 相关的词。这项是预读时就预警过的「海岛+seafood」刻板印象陷阱——主体考生容易凭「海岛大概有好吃的海鲜」这种常识脑补出答案，但原文没说就是没说。
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：原文提及 coast（located off the southeast coast of Spain）只是说岛「位于西班牙东南海岸外」，是定位用语，不是描述岛本身的海岸线独特。选项 Its unusual coastline 借了 coast 这个原词，并加了一个原文没有的形容词 unusual。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：原文通篇没有提到岛上有什么建筑（无任何 building / architecture / house 的描述），与选项 Its architecture 完全无对应原文。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（its unspoiled beaches and crystal clear waters ↔ Its unspoiled beaches 原词原音直接复现）

questions.evidenceText: For decades tourists have been flocking to Palmador, which is located off the southeast coast of Spain. They come to enjoy its unspoiled beaches and crystal clear waters.

questions.stem: What do estate agents say about Palmador?

options.text: It is worth over 18 million euros.
It has beautiful weather all year round.
It is an ideal place to meet famous stars.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：It is said to have a remarkable location that few other private islands of this size can match, according to estate agents.信号：引述标志 according to + 最高级语义 。答案信号有两层：①引述定位词 according to estate agents 与题干 estate agents say 完全对应——这是这道题答案句的硬信…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：18 million euros 确实出现在原音里（bought by a family from Europe for 18 million euros），但它是新闻导语里的成交价格，不是房产中介对这座岛的评价。预读时就把 18 million euros 标为数字陷阱预警——正是为这一题做准备。 借用原文：its seafront is public land and is a favorite destination for famous people
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：全文没有出现 weather / climate / sunshine 等任何与天气有关的描述。选项 beautiful weather all year round 是基于「度假胜地通常天气好」做的常识脑补，并不来自原音。
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：原文 its seafront is public land and is a favorite destination for famous people 说海滨是「名人爱来的地方」，但这与选项 an ideal place to meet famous stars（一个见明星的理想场所）不同——前者讲名人来此度假，后者讲普通人来此能「遇见」明星。同时该句也不是 estate agents 说的，而是新闻自己的陈述，连发话人都对不上。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a remarkable location that few other private islands of this size can match ↔ It has an unmatched location 最高级语义·同义浓缩）

questions.evidenceText: It is said to have a remarkable location that few other private islands of this size can match, according to estate agents.

transcript.text: M: Hi, Christie's Gym Center. How can I help you?
transcript.zh: M: 你好, Christie's健身中心。有什么可以帮您的?

transcript.text: W: Hi, I'm calling to ask about the newly scheduled gym classes. I'm just wondering if I can get a discount on them.
transcript.zh: W: 你好,我打电话是想问一下新安排的健身课程。我想知道能不能打折。

transcript.text: M: Are you already a member?
transcript.zh: M: 您已经是会员了吗?

transcript.text: W: Yes, I signed up two months ago, but I haven't been to any of the group classes yet.
transcript.zh: W: 是的,我两个月前注册的,但还没参加过任何团体课程。

transcript.text: M: Can I take your name please?
transcript.zh: M: 能告诉我您的名字吗?

transcript.text: W: Yes. My name is Carol Friedman.
transcript.zh: W: 可以。我叫Carol Friedman。

transcript.text: M: Carol Friedman. That's right. And you signed up two months ago. Currently we are offering existing members discounts off two of our brand new classes, hot yoga, and advanced spinning, but the discount doesn't apply to any of our regular classes I'm afraid.
transcript.zh: M: Carol Friedman。没错。您两个月前注册的。目前我们给现有会员提供两门全新课程的折扣,高温瑜伽和高级动感单车,但折扣恐怕不适用于我们的常规课程。

transcript.text: W: I'm only interested in the new classes. So how much of a discount is there on these two new classes?
transcript.zh: W: 我只对新课程感兴趣。那这两门新课程有多少折扣?

transcript.text: M: The same discount of 20% is being offered to everyone at the door on a "first come, first served" basis for the first month. It's a shame you missed out on the general discount.
transcript.zh: M: 第一个月所有人在门口都能享受同样的8折优惠,先到先得。很遗憾您错过了普遍折扣。

transcript.text: W: I see.
transcript.zh: W: 我明白了。

transcript.text: M: But you can get 25% off if you sign up in advance. Which of the two classes are you thinking about?

transcript.text: A new study has demonstrated the importance of women's rights. The researchers behind the study state that many parts of the world have made good economic progress, but women's rights are often overlooked. Thus, they wanted to determine if there was a link between protection of women's rights and public health.
transcript.zh: 一项新研究证明了女性权利的重要性。该研究的研究人员指出,世界许多地区取得了良好的经济进步,但女性权利往往被忽视。因此,他们想确定女性权利保护与公共健康之间是否存在联系。

transcript.text: The researchers analyzed databases which held information from 162 countries for the period 2004 to 2010.
transcript.zh: 研究人员分析了包含162个国家2004年至2010年期间信息的数据库。

transcript.text: Countries were classified according to the respect they gave to women's economic and social rights. There were three categories. They were high, moderate, and poor.
transcript.zh: 各国根据其对女性经济和社会权利的尊重程度进行分类。分为三个类别:高、中等和低。

transcript.text: Analysis of the data showed that countries with strong women's rights had better health than those where women's rights were not as respected.
transcript.zh: 数据分析显示,女性权利保障强的国家比那些不太尊重女性权利的国家拥有更好的健康状况。

transcript.text: The health indicators studied included disease prevention, reproductive health, death rates, and life expectancy.
transcript.zh: 研究的健康指标包括疾病预防、生殖健康、死亡率和预期寿命。

transcript.text: Furthermore, in countries where women's rights were most respected, but where access to hospitals and doctors was below average, health outcomes were still better than in countries rated as moderate or poor. This confirms that even with a lack of resources, if a country has strong women's rights, the health outcomes are better.
transcript.zh: 此外,在最尊重女性权利但医院和医生资源低于平均水平的国家,健康结果仍然优于被评为中等或低的国家。这证实了即使在资源匮乏的情况下,如果一个国家拥有强有力的女性权利保障,健康结果也会更好。

transcript.text: Thus, the researchers argued that gender equality is not just a women's rights issue. It is also a development issue. This is because better health aids economic development. They note that the value of women's rights has often been questioned from an economic standpoint. Some have argued that ensuring those rights would limit progress, but this study indicates the opposite.
transcript.zh: 因此,研究人员认为性别平等不仅仅是女性权利问题,也是发展问题。这是因为更好的健康状况有助于经济发展。他们指出,女性权利的价值常常从经济角度受到质疑。有些人认为确保这些权利会限制进步,但这项研究表明情况恰恰相反。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A few years ago I found myself teaching a university class on evil. It was for third-year criminology students to help them contextualize theory and research within controversial current topics. It was a huge success. The debates were heated and interesting. I could see people's views change within the course of a single lecture. Over the past 13 years, as a student, lecturer and researcher, I've enjoyed discussing the science of evil with anyone willing to listen. What I like most is destroying the cliche(陈词滥调) of good and evil, and replacing them with scientific insight. We need a more informed way of discussing behavior that at first we cannot, or should not, begin to understand.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Without understanding, we risk dehumanizing others, writing off human beings simply because we don't comprehend them. We must try to understand what we have labeled evil. We tend to think evil is something that other people are. We think of ourselves as "good people", and even when we do morally wrong things, we understand the context of our decisions. With others, however, it is far easier to write them off. If their actions deviate(偏离) substantially from what we consider acceptable, we may label them evil. We need to be careful with this. Calling someone evil is often similar to saying they cannot change, and perhaps aren't even a human at all. However, when you actually go monster-hunting, and you look deeply at the people behind shocking behavior, you may be surprised.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: As a child I used to love the Scooby-Doo cartoons. Arriving in their "Mystery Machine", the gang would have to find a monster who was terrorizing a neighborhood. They would run around looking for clues and at the end unmask the bad guy. It was always a normal person in a costume. There were no monsters. Like the Scooby crew, we may find ourselves hunting for an easy fix, one word for people who do bad things. But if we take a good look, the word "evil" is insufficient—there are no simple explanations for why humans do bad things: instead there are many, and they are all marvelously different.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Evil is typically referred to when there is deviance from social norms: formal deviance is the violation of laws, like theft, murder, and attacks, while informal deviance involves violations of social norms, like lying. Evil behavior is typically thought to embrace one or both forms. However, deviance can also describe a behavior that simply differs from the norm.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Perhaps this is where we can find the good side of our bad side. Deviating from the norm can make us villains(恶棍), but it can also make us heroes. A child deviates from social pressures when they stand up for another child being bullied in school. A soldier deviates when they choose not to follow orders to kill an innocent civilian. An employee in a big tech company deviates when they expose its wrongdoings.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Creativity is also a deviation. Here, too, things are complex. Thinking creatively has given us modern medicine, technology and modern political structures, but it has also given us poison and nuclear weapons. Great benefit and great harm can come from the same human tendency.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: In a research paper, Evil Genius, published in 2014, the behavioral scientists Francesca Gino and Scott Wiltermuth wanted to examine whether people who behave unethically in one task are more creative than others on a subsequent task, even after controlling for differences in baseline creative skills. The unethical behavior they chose was dishonesty.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Over five experiments, researchers gave participants tasks in which they could cheat. In one study, they were given matrices(矩阵) and had to find two numbers that added up to 10. Participants were asked to self-report how well they did at the end of the study: 59% cheated by saying that they solved more matrices than they actually had.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: After each task, the researchers measured participants' performance on the Remote Associates Test. This shows participants three words at a time that appear to be unrelated, and the person has to think of a fourth word that is associated with all of them. For example, you might get "Fox, Man, Peep", or "Dust, Cereal, Fish". In order to find the linking words ("Hole" for the first, "Bowl" for the second) you need to be creative. The more you get right, the more creative you are thought to be because you have come up with uncommon associations.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: For every one of the five studies, they found the same thing—participants who cheated in the first task did better on the creativity task. Why? Like other forms of unethical behavior, lying means breaking rules. It involves being deviant, going against the social principle that people should tell the truth. Similarly, being creative involves "thinking outside the box", deviating from expectations. They involve similar thought patterns, so stimulating one stimulates the other. Can we learn from this? Perhaps. To be more creative, we could try lying in a controlled environment. Find online logic games and cheat at them, play Scrabble(拼字游戏) with a dictionary, or write a story about something that is untrue? Such tasks can get our brains thinking flexibly, beyond our normal comfort zone. This is not a call to become a compulsive(强迫性的) liar, but a controlled liar.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: In addition to benefits for creativity, deviance can be a good thing in other ways. Even Philip Zimbardo, the author of the Stanford prison experiment, who showed how easily we can be led to behave badly, believes that the future of deviance research may lie more in understanding extreme pro-social behavior, such as heroism. Like evil, we often view heroism as only a possibility for outliers—for people who are abnormal. But Zimbardo asks: "What if the capability to act heroically is also fundamentally ordinary and available to all of us?" Some say we should never meet our heroes, lest they disappoint us when we find out how normal they are. But this should be liberating, not disappointing. We are all capable of behaving like outliers. It's time for us to understand deviance, and realize its potential for good as well as for harm.

questions.analysis:
【参考译文】
The Winter Solstice is the day on which daytime is the shortest and night is the longest in the whole year, marking the beginning of the coldest period of the year. After the Winter Solstice, the temperature drops lower and lower, and people's outdoor activities gradually decrease. Since there is not much work to do in the fields, farmers are mainly busy with maintaining the irrigation system and protecting crops from freezing, while preparing for next spring's sowing. Chinese people have always attached great importance to the Winter Solstice and regard it as a festival in many places, though the ways of celebrating it vary from place to place. Northerners have the custom of eating jiaozi on the Winter Solstice, while Southerners have the tradition of eating tangyuan on this day.
